correctness.rationale: For arbitrary existing thick GQ(s,t), the incidence distances are 1/3 for point–line, 2/4 for same-part pairs. A complete neighbor-by-neighbor case analysis proves MMD iff the same-shore pair is at distance four. The cited general strong-resolving/vertex-cover equivalence then reduces all strong sets to independent omissions in the two complementary collinearity graphs. The GQ uniqueness axiom forces every pairwise-collinear point set (size≥2) into one line and every pairwise-concurrent line family into a pencil. This proves the enumerator factors and that all maximal omissions have sizes (s+1,t+1), yielding strong dimension st(s+t+2) and N_P N_L bases. Coordinate replacement costs s/s+1 and t/t+1 give the sharp max(s,t) connectivity threshold. At threshold no mixed-coordinate move is possible, and GQ collinearity/intersection graphs have diameter two, so the Cartesian-product radius/diameter is exactly 4 (equal orders) or 3 (unequal). Python verifies GQ axioms, all MMD pairs, full shore enumerators and exchange components for (2,2),(2,4); independent C++ constructs the (2,2) quadrangle from duads and synthemes and checks all 593775 possible six-omission candidates, exchange edges and diameter. No infinite assertion is based on finite experiments.

value.rationale: A complete structural classification of all strong landmark sets for an infinite design-theoretic class is an exact natural invariant, with a factored all-cardinality polynomial rather than a single extremal number. It proves all inclusion-minimal strong resolving sets are also globally minimum, a nontrivial purity property, and determines precisely when optimal placements become exchange-connected without additional landmarks. Different symmetric and asymmetric order pairs yield provably different transition graph metrics. The uniform result has natural use as a benchmark for geometric localization and basis-reconfiguration algorithms; it is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a numerical recomputation.
